html:
The Madaba Map is a mosaic map on the floor of a church in Madaba, Jordan, made in the 6th century. It is the oldest surviving map of the Holy Land.

It shows the lands from Lebanon to Egypt, with the Jordan river, the Dead Sea with boats on it, and more than a hundred towns, labelled in Greek. Its centre is a detailed picture of Jerusalem, with its walls, gates, main street and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

The mosaic was rediscovered in 1884 when a new church was built on the ruins. Large parts are lost, but it is still a key source for the towns of Byzantine Palestine. Madaba was a Christian town with many mosaics. See also Jordan.
sum: The Madaba Map is a mosaic map on the floor of a church in Madaba, Jordan, made in the 6th century. It is the oldest surviving map of the Holy Land.
